items.stem: A hotspot is best described as:

options.text: A boundary where two plates collide and one sinks
A fixed point in the mantle where heat rises and melts through the crust above
A trench where ocean crust is destroyed
A crack where a continent is splitting apart

items.explanation: A hotspot is a point on the crust directly above a fixed mantle plume. Heat rises there and melts through the plate, even in the middle of a plate.

items.stem: Most of Earth's volcanoes form at plate boundaries. Where do the Hawaiian Islands sit?

options.text: Along a deep-sea subduction trench
At a divergent mid-ocean ridge
On the edge of the Pacific plate
In the middle of the Pacific plate

items.explanation: The Hawaiian Islands sit in the middle of the Pacific plate, far from any boundary. That is what makes them hotspot volcanoes.

items.stem: As the Pacific plate moves over the fixed hotspot, what happens to the volcanoes it carries?

options.text: Each volcano is carried away from the hotspot and a new one forms, building a chain
Every volcano stays over the hotspot and keeps growing taller
The volcanoes drag the hotspot along with them
The volcanoes sink the moment they form

items.explanation: The plate moves while the hotspot stays fixed, so each volcano drifts off the heat and a new one grows in its place. Repeated over time, this builds an island chain.

items.stem: In a hotspot island chain, which island is the youngest?

options.text: The one farthest from the hotspot
They are all exactly the same age
The one sitting directly over the hotspot
The one that has already become a seamount

items.explanation: New volcanoes form over the hotspot, so the island sitting over it is the youngest. Islands get older with distance from the hotspot.

items.stem: On the Big Island of Hawaii the volcanoes are active, but the islands to the northwest are quiet. Why?

options.text: The northwest islands were built by a completely different hotspot
The northwest islands have drifted off the hotspot and lost their magma source
The northwest islands are actually much younger
The hotspot itself slowly moved to the northwest

items.explanation: The northwest islands have been carried away from the hotspot. Cut off from the plume's magma, their volcanoes went extinct, while the Big Island still sits over the heat.

items.stem: The Pacific plate moves toward the northwest, and the islands grow older in that direction. Compared to the oldest islands, where is the hotspot today?

options.text: To the southeast, where the youngest islands and Loihi are
To the northwest, beneath the oldest islands
Directly under the single oldest island
There is no consistent pattern to the island ages

items.explanation: The youngest, active volcanoes mark the hotspot. Since the plate moves northwest, the hotspot is at the southeast end, near the Big Island and Loihi.

items.stem: An underwater mountain that was once a volcanic island above the sea is called a:

options.text: Mid-ocean ridge
Rift valley
Subduction trench
Seamount

items.explanation: A seamount is a submerged, extinct volcanic island. Old hotspot islands sink and become seamounts as the crust they ride on cools and subsides.

items.stem: Why do old hotspot islands slowly sink below the ocean surface over millions of years?

options.text: The hotspot reaches up and pulls them down as it cools
As the crust moves away from the hotspot it cools, becomes more dense, and subsides
Rising sea levels bury them within a single year
Newer islands physically push them underwater

items.explanation: Crust that moves away from the hotspot cools and grows denser. Denser crust rides lower, so the old islands subside, and erosion wears them down into seamounts.

items.stem: Loihi (Kamaehuakanaloa) is an undersea volcano just southeast of the Big Island. What does it most likely represent?

options.text: The oldest volcano in the entire chain
A volcano formed at a subduction zone
The next Hawaiian island, now forming over the hotspot
A seamount that has finished sinking

items.explanation: Loihi sits over the hotspot at the southeast end of the chain, so it is the youngest volcano and the likely next Hawaiian island.

items.stem: How does a hotspot island chain provide evidence that a tectonic plate has moved?

options.text: The line of islands and their ages record the direction and path the plate traveled over the fixed hotspot
The islands all erupted at once, proving the plate never moves
The islands show that the hotspot moves while the plate stays still
The islands prove that volcanoes can only form at plate boundaries

items.explanation: Because the hotspot stays fixed, the chain records plate motion. The order and ages of the islands trace the direction the plate has traveled.
